discovery: Optical cavity quantum electrodynamics and the quantum-network paradigm: coherent transfer of quantum states between single atoms and single photons

nominees.name: Gerhard Rempe
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

subfield: Quantum optics / atomic physics (quantum networks, light-matter interfaces)
motivation: Kimble and Rempe pioneered strong coupling between single atoms and optical photons in high-finesse cavities, turning cavity QED from a thought experiment into a quantitative light-matter interface: vacuum Rabi splitting, single-atom trapping, deterministic single-photon sources and photon blockade. Cirac, with Zoller, Kimble and Mabuchi, proposed in 1997 the protocol for coherent quantum state transfer between distant atomic nodes via photons, founding the quantum-network concept, and with Duan, Lukin and Zoller the ensemble-based quantum repeater. Their experiments then realized it: atom-photon entanglement, state transfer and teleportation between remote single-atom nodes, heralded entanglement of memories, and quantum memories for light. This body of work defines the elementary building blocks of the quantum internet, now pursued worldwide and by industry. It opened a genuinely new capability: faithfully mapping quantum information between stationary matter and flying photons.
